grades.quote: Either you have some way to know that only one is waiting, or you know that only one would be able to proceed, with the others looping back to waiting.
grades.reason: Discusses notify vs notifyAll and mentions waiters looping back to waiting, but doesn't explain why the wait itself should be in a while loop. This is only tangential support.
Introduces condition variables and why threads need to wait, but does not address the while loop.

grades.quote: Second, the waiting is done in a loop; only when the waited-for condition has been verified to hold does the method move on to its real work. The loop is essential because an awoken thread needs to reacquire the mutex, contending with any other threads that are also trying to acquire the mutex. There is no guarantee that the awoken thread will get the mutex first. As such, there is no guarantee what state it will find; it may need to wait again.
grades.reason: Directly explains that the wait is in a loop because an awakened thread must reacquire the mutex and compete with other threads. It may find the condition no longer holds, so it needs to re-check and possibly wait again.
